EXAMPLE COMMUNITY HOSPITAL - EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT
TRIAGE RECORD
Patient: TESTPATIENT, ALEX   DOB 01/01/1980   Arrival 07/19/2024 21:40
Mode: private vehicle. Chief complaint: low back pain after lifting a box at work, onset 2 hours ago.
Pain 7/10, no numbness, no bowel or bladder change. BP 138/86 HR 92 RR 16 SpO2 99%. ESI level 4.

label: ed_note
text:
denies prior back surgery. Exam: paraspinal tenderness L4-S1 bilaterally, straight leg raise negative,
strength 5/5 both legs, reflexes symmetric. No midline tenderness.
MDM: mechanical low back strain, no red flags. No imaging indicated per clinical criteria.
Plan: ibuprofen 600 mg, cyclobenzaprine 5 mg at bedtime, heat.

label: ed_note
text:
DISCHARGE INSTRUCTIONS - TESTPATIENT, ALEX
Diagnosis: acute low back strain.
Take ibuprofen 600 mg every 8 hours with food for 5 days. Cyclobenzaprine 5 mg at bedtime as needed, may cause drowsiness.
Return if you develop leg weakness, numbness, or loss of bladder control.
Follow up with occupational health in 3-5 days. Work note: light duty, no lifting over 10 lb.

label: education_handout
text:
BACK STRAIN: WHAT TO EXPECT
Most back strains improve within two to six weeks. Staying gently active helps more than bed rest.
Apply heat for 15-20 minutes at a time. Lift with your legs, keep loads close to your body.
Call your doctor if pain spreads down a leg or you have new weakness.
